evals.name: new-swiftui-app-delivery
evals.prompt: Build a polished SwiftUI todo app in this existing Xcode project. It should persist tasks, animate smoothly, support accessibility, and run in Simulator.
evals.expected_output: An end-to-end implementation that inspects the project first, selects only relevant specialist skills, uses clear product/domain naming and feature boundaries, preserves project settings, and verifies build, persistence, accessibility, motion, and Simulator behavior.
assertions: Inspects the existing project, target, deployment version, architecture, and Git state before broad edits.
Loads only relevant SwiftUI, persistence, accessibility, testing, and Simulator guidance rather than all installed skills.
Uses discoverable app/feature naming and avoids leaving the app in one generic ContentView file.
Builds the actual target and exercises the primary flow in Simulator.
Verifies persistence across relaunch and provides Reduce Motion/accessibility behavior.

evals.name: focused-concurrency-boundary
evals.prompt: Fix this one Swift 6 Sendable compiler error in my networking callback.
evals.expected_output: A boundary-aware response that routes to swift-concurrency and does not invoke a broad app-delivery refactor.
assertions: Treats the request as a focused diagnostic rather than an end-to-end app workflow.
Does not reorganize project files, add unrelated UI, or load the full iOS skill set.
Preserves behavior and applies the smallest concurrency-safe fix.

evals.name: behavior-preserving-refactor
evals.prompt: Refactor a 500-line SwiftUI dashboard into sensible files without changing how it looks or behaves.
evals.expected_output: A structure-only refactor that pins behavior, uses role-based filenames and real View boundaries, preserves state and side-effect timing, and compares the same build/preview/simulator fixture afterward.
assertions: Records layout, navigation, identity, accessibility, persistence, animation, and side-effect behavior as the refactor contract.
Extracts meaningful dedicated views rather than only computed properties, extensions, or arbitrary one-line files.
Matches filenames to primary types and uses product/domain-role naming.
Builds and visually exercises the refactored screen using the same fixture.

evals.name: deployment-target-preservation
evals.prompt: Add an iOS 26 visual effect to an app whose minimum deployment target is iOS 17.
evals.expected_output: An availability-aware implementation that keeps iOS 17 support, verifies the API against the installed SDK or primary sources, and provides an appropriate fallback instead of silently raising the target.
assertions: Inspects and preserves the existing iOS 17 deployment target.
Gates the iOS 26 API and supplies a behaviorally appropriate fallback.
Does not change project-wide platform settings without explicit authorization.
Builds or otherwise verifies both the modern path and compatibility assumptions.
